title: Winners of Bird Photographer of the Year Revealed
paragraphs: The winners of the Bird Photographer of the Year 2026 competition have been announced, with the top prize going to a dramatic underwater image of a seabird diving for food.

The overall winner was British photographer Henley Spiers, for an image called "Sunball Rocket." The photo shows a northern gannet, a large seabird, diving underwater like a torpedo, lit by sunlight shining through the water. It was taken just after the bird broke through the surface of the sea. Spiers received a prize of £3,000.

According to Spiers, when gannets spot fish, they fly into the wind and use their wings as brakes. Once they begin to dive, they turn into a "pointed torpedo" and can enter the water at speeds of up to 86 kilometers per hour.

The competition received more than 24,000 entries this year. The title of Young Bird Photographer of the Year went to Parham Pourahmad, a 16-year-old from the United States. His winning image, "Moonlit Night," shows a great horned owl as a dark shape against a glowing full moon. Pourahmad took the picture in a park near his home.

Other winning images included "I'm Keeping Everyone Dry" by Donald Chin, which shows an adult bird protecting its chicks under its open wings, and "Eye-to-Eye with a Short-Eared Owl" by Ivan Sjögren, in which an owl flies straight toward the camera. Another winner, "Radiant" by Thomas Deliberto, shows a male greater sage-grouse spreading its tail feathers as the sun rises behind it in the US state of Utah.

The competition also supports bird conservation. This year, it donated more than £5,000 to Birds on the Brink, an organization that supports small bird conservation projects. The winning photos will also be published in a book.
Will Nicholls, the competition's director, said the winning images remind people of the value of authentic photography, especially as more and more images are now created by artificial intelligence.
